accuracy.evidence: Values D 500 and M 1000, the six subtractive pairs (IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, CM), the three-in-a-row limit and the never-doubled V, L and D were checked against Encyclopaedia Britannica's 'Roman numeral' entry and the Year 5 programme of study. roman() and value() in learn/romanm_art.js were run in Node on every number used: 1999 = MCMXCIX, 847 = DCCCXLVII, 2024 = MMXXIV, 444 = CDXLIV, 1066 = MLXVI, 1485 = MCDLXXXV, 999 = CMXCIX, 990 = CMXC, MCMLXXXIV = 1984, DCCCLXXXVIII = 888, CDXC = 490, DX = 510, MMXIX = 2019, all canonical. Parameterised answers (1000+100a+10b, 1900+10a+b, 500+100a+b, 2000+10a+b) are whole numbers at every corner.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the Year 5 slips NCETM and teachers report: adding every symbol (MCMXCIX as 2221 in p3 and challenge tag add; MMXXIV as 2026 in m5), CCCC for 400 (first predict, tray message 'Never four Cs in a row', p4, challenge tag four), invented pairs IM, XM, DM and MIM (robot sayings 1, 5 and 6, year predict 'Which is 1999? MIM or MCMXCIX', m4, m7, challenge tag pair), reading CD as 600 (robot saying 3, challenge tag flip), splitting a pair across chunks (split-scene message 'CM belong together'), letters treated as digits (20024, tag digit) and longer means bigger (compare scene, p5, tag long).

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab is about reading and writing numerals up to M: hundreds are built from C, D and M tiles, long numerals such as MCMXCIX and DCCCXLVII are split by tapping the gaps between place-value chunks, years are dialled with four thousands/hundreds/tens/ones columns that each show their Roman chunk, and pairs are compared where the longer numeral is smaller. flagroman (959, to 100) builds 1 to 100 from I, V, X, L and C tiles and judges classmates; it has no D or M, no chunk splitting, no year dial and no length trap. The lab_distinct gate keeps flag_romanm.js under 30% similar to every other lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the structure by doing: the year dial's readout shows 'MLXX = 1070' as columns change and turns green only when the year matches, and the success line lists the chunks ('1999 is MCMXCIX, written one place at a time: M, CM, XC, IX'). In the split scene a cut inside CM is drawn as a dashed red line with 'CM belong together: C before M takes away, so CM is 900', and the found chunks are listed with their values. If the learner starts 900 with M, the tray turns red with 'M is 1000, more than 900. Tap the tray to take the last tile off.'

predictions.evidence: Three predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the scene disproves: 'How is 400 written?' (CCCC) before building CD; 'Which is 1999?' (MIM, a well-known wrong form) before dialling MCMXCIX column by column; 'Which is bigger: DCCCLXXXVIII or M?' (the longer one) before the compare scene shows 888 against 1000. The finish line reveals the learner's own prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions with two tagged wrong answers each; slipMsg() gives nine distinct messages: add (a smaller symbol before a bigger one is taken away), chunk (CM is 900, not 1100), four (never four in a row), flip (DC 600 v CD 400), pair (only six take-away pairs; X cannot go before M), long (length is not value), same (888 is less than 1000), digit (letters are not place-value digits) and sym (D 500, L 50, M 1000).

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences with worked numbers (CD is 500 take away 100, which is 400) and pass the learner kid FK limit; adult paragraphs were rewritten into shorter sentences and pass the adult limit in validate_lessons.py. Numerals use a serif face at 22 to 30 px; labels are dark on white or cream and shrink to fit at 360 px.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph adds one idea: the two new symbols, the take-away pairs with CD and CM, chunking to read MCMXCIX, and writing a year plus the length trap. The adult text gives the Year 5 requirement, the full rule set and the digit-to-chunk link, seven named mistakes with what to ask, and what the lab does. The content gate found no filler and under 12% overlap with every lesson, including Roman numerals to 100.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots (dark theme) of every step at rest and part-way through Show me: the C, D and M tiles are about 100 x 75 px, the nine letter tiles of DCCCXLVII fit across with tap-anywhere-near-a-gap cutting, the four year columns are about 85 px wide with up and down halves, and the compare cards span the width. Every canvas action also has a button under the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button: C, D and M ('Add D, 500') and Undo; one button per gap in the split scene ('Cut between letter 2 C and letter 3 M'); Thousands, Hundreds, Tens and Ones up and down; each numeral in the compare scene; Right or Slip. Each change is announced through c.say and the canvas aria-label, and challenge feedback is a polite live region. Right and wrong are marked with text and ticks, not colour alone. The walk gate's axe run is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
